transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Samir Gupta (NovaPay), Lena Ortiz (NovaPay), Mark Reynolds (NovaPay)

Summary:
Quick check-in on the POC throughput tuning work: results from last week's microbench, validate continuous batching changes, set concurrency target and queueing behavior for the next run, agree on next steps and infra deep-dive.

Topics:
- Continuous batching config changes (prefix caching, batch windows)
- Concurrency targets and observed tail latency
- Queueing vs throttling tradeoffs
- Cost/latency tradeoffs and dedicated vs hosted considerations

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey folks, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick sync on the throughput optim work and last week's runs. How's every \u0004 everyone doing?
[00:06] Samir Gupta: Good, thanks. We've been waiting to see the, ah, the results you mentioned, Alex. The microbench you ran with the new batching windows.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yeah, hi. Quick note, some of the numbers in the spreadsheet are from the k-v cache change plus the bump to 80ms batch window, so keep that in mind.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: Cool. Also want to call out our target is 1800 qps for peak promo events with p99 < 450ms, that's what product cares about.
[00:28] Mark Reynolds: And cost threshold \u0004 we can't exceed our committed spend estimate by more than 15% during POC.
[00:34] Alex Chen: Got it. Ok so quick walk through: last week's microbench (link: https://redwood.link/benchmarks/novapay-2026-04-18.csv) showed overall token throughput improved about 27% with continuous batching enabled, but p99 latency saw sporadic spikes when concurrency hit the queueing threshold.
[00:50] Priya Patel: To add, the continuous batching helped because similar sequence lengths grouped better and the KV cache hit rate increased from ~63% to ~78%, that reduced decode cycles. But we noticed a coupling between batch window and the runtime's kernel selection \u0004 some batches triggered less optimal kernels for long-seq, causing those spikes.
[01:12] Samir Gupta: Wait, less optimal kernels? Like why would a different kernel cause a spike \u0004 shouldn't the runtime pick best?
[01:18] Priya Patel: It should, but when the batch composition changes with more long-context tokens mixed in, the heuristic in the local scheduler picked the single-threaded kernel for those batches. We're proposing a small scheduler tweak to bias towards vectorized kernels when average seq len is above a threshold.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: That makes sense. Is that a config flip or code change?
[01:40] Priya Patel: It's a code change \u0004 small change in scheduler heuristics; we can ship as a tunable flag for POC.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: There's a potential risk rolling code on the private infra \u0004 we'll coordinate with NovaPay SREs.
[01:52] Mark Reynolds: We prefer config-first if possible. Code changes ok for POC but need clear rollback.
[01:58] Alex Chen: Absolutely. For next run we're planning three parallel experiments: 1) Increase batch window from 80ms -> 120ms and test. 2) Add scheduler bias flag to prefer vectorized kernels for avg seq len > 512. 3) Introduce concurrency shaper at the frontdoor \u0004 queueing policy change from unlimited queue to bounded queue with backpressure based on latency SLO.
[02:21] Samir Gupta: For the queueing policy \u0004 can you explain bounded queue vs the throttling approach you mentioned earlier?
[02:26] Priya Patel: Sure, bounded queue means we accept up to N in-flight requests in the platform queue, beyond that we return 429 or push back to caller. Throttling means we slow acceptance rate to keep the runtime under target concurrency by pacing. Bounded queue gives better tail predictability but fails fast which your app needs to handle.
[02:44] Samir Gupta: Hmm our client side currently retries on 5xx, not on 429 specifically; we'll need to tweak our SDK logic to treat 429 as retryable-after. That so we don't see client retries thundering.
[02:55] Alex Chen: Good catch. We can add headers to indicate Retry-After windows and help with guidance.
[03:00] Lena Ortiz: What about the KV cache warm-up \u0004 we noticed cold-starts at the start of peak windows. Can continuous batching help warm the cache faster?
[03:07] Priya Patel: It helps if request distribution has repeated prefixes. We also support proactive pre-population by replaying recent top prompts into the cache; Redwood can run a warm-up job at the start of the window.
[03:18] Samir Gupta: Yes please, we'll share top-100 prompt set.
[03:21] Alex Chen: Noted (Samir will share prompts).
[03:24] [03:24] Alex Chen: Quick numbers from the CSV \u0004 baseline (no continuous batching, window 0) p50=92ms p95=310ms p99=720ms at 1200 concurrent tokens/sec. With CB at 80ms we saw p50=75ms p95=250ms p99=640ms at same load, and at 1600 c we see p99 jump to ~980ms in one run.
[03:46] Priya Patel: The jump aligns with a batch composition anomaly where long seqs and short seqs mixed and produced large KV miss penalties. We're adding a pre-binning step to avoid mixing >1024 token sequences with <128 in same batch.
[04:01] Samir Gupta: Pre-binning seems ok. Does it reduce batch utilization?
[04:05] Priya Patel: Slightly, but overall reduces worst-case time. Binning also lets us select specialized kernels per bin, which reduces variance.
[04:14] Mark Reynolds: Curious about cost impact \u0004 if we do more bins and smaller batches, won't that increase per-token cost?
[04:20] Alex Chen: There's tradeoff \u0004 better tail latency can require slightly higher cost per token since batching efficiency drops, but we can compensate by using quantized model variants for certain traffic segments or enabling burst capacity only for peak windows. We'll model both options and include estimated unit costs.
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: Ok, we need the cost model. Can you include worst-case and typical-case numbers?
[04:39] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll send a calc. Expect approx +6-12% cost in worst-case for strict binning with smaller batch sizes; with kernel bias and warm-up we hope net cost delta is <5%.
[04:51] Priya Patel: One more note: we saw GPU utilization at 86% on the dedicated pool but tail latency correlated with host-level memory thrashing on a couple nodes; we're recommending slight bump in reserved mem parameter and pinning the runtime to fewer allocs. That is a config change not infra re-provision.
[05:10] Samir Gupta: We'll need SRE sign-off \u0004 I'll loop them in.
[05:13] Alex Chen: Great. Questions from NovaPay?
[05:16] Mark Reynolds: Do we have any comparison to managed vendors re: burst behavior? You mentioned Anthropic previously.
[05:21] Priya Patel: From our public benches, managed vendors often sacrifice tail predictability at scale because they maximize batch utilization; Redwood's approach is configurable to trade batch efficiency for tail SLO which helps for NovaPay's p99 requirements. But we'll include direct comparisons in the follow-up deck.
[05:36] Samir Gupta: Ok. For the upcoming 24h run, what's the target concurrency we should shoot for? We said 1800 qps peak earlier.
[05:44] Alex Chen: For safety let's target 2000 concurrent requests in bench to induce the tails and observe behavior. That gives headroom and shows stress points.
[05:51] Samir Gupta: Sounds good. Also timeline \u0004 we want to present to execs next Friday. Will you have the results and the cost model by then?
[05:58] Alex Chen: We'll prioritize. Plan: run the 24h today/tonight, collect logs and perf traces, share results + config diff + cost modeling by 2026-04-23.
[06:07] Lena Ortiz: Can you also include a short README for our SREs on the rollback steps?
[06:11] Priya Patel: Yes, rollback is a single flag revert for the scheduler, and config revert for queueing. We'll document step-by-step and include the exact CLI commands.
[06:21] Jordan Lee: I'll coordinate the infra deep-dive and send calendar invite to NovaPay SREs \u0004 propose Wed 2026-04-22 14:00 UTC.
[06:28] Samir Gupta: That works.
[06:30] Alex Chen: Great. Any other open items?
[06:33] Mark Reynolds: One last ask \u0004 can you provide sample SDK retry guidance for 429 vs 5xx? We want to avoid retry storms.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Yup, we'll include recommended backoff windows and header usage.
[06:44] Priya Patel: Also will include example configs for batch window and bin thresholds.
[06:48] Alex Chen: Cool. Recap of next steps: Alex to run 24h benchmark at 2000 concurrency and share logs by 4/23; Priya to prepare scheduler bias toggle and example config; Samir to share top-100 prompts and traffic trace; Jordan to schedule infra deep-dive; Redwood to share cost model and rollback README.
[07:04] Samir Gupta: Thanks everyone.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: Thanks.
[07:07] Mark Reynolds: Thanks all.
[07:09] Alex Chen: End call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker label overlap and a few mis-transcriptions (e.g., "k-v" vs KV, Redwood product names slightly garbled), silence gaps trimmed.
